findings: The older broad-market evidence used simple_v1 and was not sufficient to answer the current-policy question, so both candidates were replayed on frozen simple_v2 through 20231231.
Replacing the sector-derived market state with five-index trend/volatility plus all-A breadth returned -11.61%, exceeded 20% drawdown and had only two positive years.
Signal-date-aligned descriptive attribution showed conditional separation, but it was not causal evidence; an earlier return-date join was discarded and disclosed.
Using broad-market extremes only as an absolute-exposure overlay improved the worst year and turnover, but changed the holding path and reduced cumulative return to -2.82%.

Five-index trend/volatility plus SW L1 breadth was materially better at +15.39% with five positive years, but still lagged the +23.31% baseline and missed the worst-year floor by 0.20 percentage point.
True broad-market inputs remain useful diagnostics, but neither tested use improved the investable product.
runtime_note: One isolated replay terminated in the known Windows/Pandas native merge layer; a fresh one-thread process completed successfully and only the complete result was retained.
next_step: Keep formal sector-breadth exposure unchanged. Publish the current and complete SW L1 broad-market state as a separate diagnostic, and do not tune broad-market thresholds or exposure mappings.
